[Thinking]
**Creating response templates**

I need to provide samples for acknowledging receipt with different tones: formal, semi-formal, and casual. I should include scenarios like delayed response, scheduling, and confirming attachments. Tips on elements like subject lines, key points, next steps, and signatures will be useful. The user likely wants templates, so I'll create a concise guide and several examples, including variations for meeting requests, received documents, and out-of-office responses. Keeping it brief and straightforward sounds good!
[/Thinking]

Here are quick, copy-ready templates to acknowledge an email, depending on the situation. Pick the tone that fits your context.

General receipt
- Formal: Thank you for your email. I acknowledge receipt and will review the details. I will get back to you by [date/time].
- Neutral: Thanks for your message—I’ve received it and will follow up by [date/time].
- Casual: Got it—thanks! I’ll take a look and circle back by [date/time].

If you need more time
- Formal: Thank you for reaching out. I’ve received your email and will need a bit of time to look into this. I’ll update you by [date/time].
- Neutral: Received—thanks. I’m looking into it and will get back to you by [date/time].

Confirming attachments or documents
- Formal: Thank you. I confirm that I’ve received the [document name(s)] attached. I’ll review and revert by [date/time].
- Neutral: Received the attachments—thanks. I’ll review and follow up by [date/time].
- If missing: Thanks for your email. It looks like the attachment didn’t come through. Could you please resend?

Acknowledging a request with next steps
- Formal: Thank you for your request. I’ve received it and will coordinate with [team/person]. Expect an update by [date/time].
- Neutral: Got your request—thanks. I’ll check with the team and get back to you by [date/time].

Meeting-related
- Accepting: Thanks for the invite. I’ve received it and accepted—see you on [date/time].
- Proposing time: Thanks for your email. I’m available on [options]. Please let me know what works for you.
- Need agenda/details: Thanks for setting this up. Could you share a brief agenda or objectives?

If you’re not the right person
- Formal: Thank you for your email. I’m not the appropriate contact for this. I’ve cc’d [Name/Team] who can assist further.
- Neutral: Thanks for reaching out. I’m not the right person, but [Name/Team] can help—adding them here.

After a mistake or delay
- Delay: My apologies for the delayed response. Thank you for your patience—I’ve reviewed your email and will follow up by [date/time].
- Correction: Thanks for flagging this. Acknowledged—I’m correcting [issue] and will confirm once resolved.

Customer/client acknowledgment
- Formal: Thank you for contacting [Company]. We’ve received your message (Ref: [ID]) and a member of our team will respond within [timeframe].
- Neutral: We’ve got your request—thanks. Ticket [ID] is open; we’ll update you within [timeframe].

Out-of-office style acknowledgment
- Short: Thanks for your email. I’m currently out of office until [date]. For urgent matters, please contact [Name, email/phone].

Tips
- Reply promptly (even if just to set expectations).
- Echo any key detail so the sender knows you read it (e.g., “regarding the Q3 budget draft”).
- Provide a clear next step and timeline.
- Keep the subject line intact unless you need a new thread.
- Use a clear sign-off: Best regards, Kind regards, Thanks, etc.

If you share your exact scenario (tone, relationship, and goal), I can tailor a one-liner you can paste in.
